display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(70, 88, 106) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p: arithmetic intensity I = useful operations / bytes moved [op/byte]

div.style: color: rgb(70, 88, 106) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p: ridge point = compute roof / measured bandwidth [op/byte]

div.style: display: table; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
is I above or below
the ridge point?

div.style: color: rgb(28, 82, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
COMPUTE-BOUND
the arithmetic units are the constraint.
More bandwidth would not help.

div.style: color: rgb(123, 36, 28) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
BANDWIDTH-BOUND
the memory system is the constraint.
More FLOPs would not help.

div.style: color: rgb(27, 58, 102) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
PREFILL
many tokens at once
each weight byte is reused across the batch
I is high

div.style: color: rgb(27, 58, 102) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
DECODE
one token at a time
each weight byte is used once per token
I is low

div.style: color: rgb(94, 61, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
So the decode levers are exactly two:
move FEWER bytes (quantize, sparsify, cache)
or move them from CLOSER (keep them resident).
